takeaway: A-delta fibres are thinly myelinated and carry pain, touch and temperature at 12-30 m/s. A-alpha is motor, A-beta touch and pressure, B pre-ganglionic autonomic, C dull ache and post-ganglionic.

question.text: Which nerve type is associated with transmitting pain, touch and temperature?

lines.text: Nerve fibres are sorted by how fast they conduct, which depends on diameter and myelin.
A alpha fibres are the big, fast, myelinated ones, for motor and proprioception.
lines.say: A alpha fibres are the big, fast, myelinated ones, for motor and proprioception.

lines.text: A beta fibres carry touch and pressure.
lines.say: A beta fibres carry touch and pressure.

lines.text: A delta fibres are thinly myelinated, and carry pain, touch and temperature.
lines.say: A delta fibres are thinly myelinated, and carry pain, touch and temperature.

lines.text: That basket of pain, touch and temperature belongs to A delta.
lines.say: That basket of pain, touch and temperature belongs to A delta.

lines.text: C fibres have no myelin at all: slow, one metre per second, carrying dull ache.
So for pain, touch and temperature, the answer is A delta.
lines.say: So for pain, touch and temperature, the answer is A delta.
